model.name: AI System
model.purpose: Govern an AI-enabled socio-technical system as a distinct operating object beyond a model artifact, including identity, intended purpose, risk class, composition, roles, lifecycle, oversight, evidence and decommissioning.
model.scope_statement: This model records a machine-based engineered system that, for explicit or implicit objectives, infers from inputs how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations or decisions that can influence physical or virtual environments, and that varies in autonomy and post-deployment adaptiveness. It covers the system as placed on a market, put into service, used under an authority, monitored, modified and retired, together with the provider-deployer value chain and the evidence needed to operate and oversee it. It does not own model-artifact internals, agent-actor personas, or incident-report case files.
in_scope: Identity, version, intended purpose, reasonably foreseeable misuse, and placement or service form of an AI system
Classification of the system by socio-technical context, task and output, and applicable regulatory risk tier including prohibited-practice screening
System-level composition of models, data and input requirements, runtime interfaces, hardware or product embedding, and optional agent surfaces
Provider, deployer, importer, distributor, authorised representative, downstream provider and product-manufacturer roles, ownership and human-oversight authority
Lifecycle from inception through verification, deployment, operation, continuous validation, re-evaluation, recall, withdrawal and retirement

Risk management, impact and fundamental-rights assessment, trustworthiness characteristics, logging, post-market monitoring, technical documentation, registration, access, retention and standards alignment
out_of_scope: Model weights, training runs, evaluation harnesses and other model artifacts as first-class records (WM-SFT-004)
Agent actor identity, goals, tools and runtime persona as first-class records (WM-AI-002)
AI incident, serious-incident or hazard case files as first-class records (WM-AI-010)
The organisation-level AI management system (AIMS) as a whole, as distinct from the AI system under that system
General-purpose AI models that have not been integrated into a system
Standalone datasets, compute clusters, or personal-data processing records except as system-level requirements and constraints
National-defence AI systems excluded by the Council of Europe Framework Convention, and other jurisdiction-specific military exclusions

boundary_notes.distinction: An AI system is a specialised engineered or machine-based system whose defining operations are inference from inputs to environment-influencing outputs, with varying autonomy and possible post-deployment adaptiveness. Ordinary software that only executes predetermined human-specified rules without such inference is out of this model and remains a generic software system.

A model is a core constituent used to make inferences; an AI system is typically built by combining one or more models with data, software, hardware and operating processes. The EU AI Act further distinguishes a general-purpose AI model from a general-purpose AI system that is based on such a model. Model internals belong in the model-artifact sibling.

ISO/IEC 22989 defines an AI agent as an automated entity that senses and responds to its environment and takes actions to achieve goals. Agents may be exposed by an AI system but are not the system record. This model only holds the system-to-agent composition link and the human-oversight surface.

Serious-incident reporting names affected AI systems; the incident case, harm narrative and regulatory notification file are not stored as the system itself. This model holds identity and linkage points so an incident can reference the governed system.

An AIMS is a set of organisational policies, processes and controls for responsible development, provision or use of AI systems. The AIMS governs many systems; this model is the governed system instance, not the management system.

A GPAI model displays significant generality and can be integrated into many downstream systems. A GPAI system is an AI system based on such a model. This model records the system side of that boundary and references the model artifact rather than duplicating GPAI model obligations.

bundles.name: Identity, definition and purpose
bundles.description: What counts as an AI system, how it is identified and versioned, and the intended purpose and misuse envelope under which it may operate.
bundles.rationale: Authoritative definitions treat the AI system, not AI as a discipline, as the actionable object. Identity and intended purpose determine every downstream obligation.

layers.name: Definition and demarcation
layers.description: Canonical definition elements that separate an AI system from ordinary software, from a model, and from an agent.

findings.name: AI system definition
findings.description: An AI system is a machine-based or engineered system that, for explicit or implicit objectives, infers from the input it receives how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations or decisions that can influence physical or virtual environments. OECD, the EU AI Act and the Council of Europe Framework Convention share this inference-centred wording; ISO/IEC 22989 uses engineered system and human-defined objectives without the verb infers.

questions.text: Which definition of AI system is adopted for this instance and how is it distinguished from ordinary rule-executing software?
Does this instance infer how to generate predictions, content, recommendations or decisions from inputs in a way that can influence physical or virtual environments?
Which definitional conflicts between OECD, EU, ISO/IEC 22989 and NIST AI RMF 1.0 are recorded for this instance rather than claimed as conformance?

data_elements.name: Adopted definition text
data_elements.description: The definition text used to admit this record as an AI system.

data_elements.name: Definition alignment codes
data_elements.description: Instruments this instance is aligned to, such as OECD-2023, EU-2024-1689 Art 3(1), ISO-22989-3.1.4, CoE-CETS-225 Art 2, NIST-AI-RMF-1.0.

data_elements.name: Output types
data_elements.description: Whether the system produces predictions, content, recommendations, decisions or other declared outputs.

data_elements.name: Environment influence
data_elements.description: Whether outputs can influence physical environments, virtual environments, or both.

artifacts.name: Definition alignment note
artifacts.description: Record of the adopted definition, aligned instruments and unresolved wording conflicts.
artifacts.identity_strategy: authoritative master-system identifier of the AI system plus definition-note revision

findings.name: Autonomy, adaptiveness and objectives
findings.description: AI systems vary in autonomy and in adaptiveness after deployment. Objectives may be explicit, implicit in rules or training data, or not fully known in advance. Post-deployment adaptation can invalidate assurances given at placement.

questions.text: What degree of autonomy is delegated to this system after humans have set its operating envelope?
answer_data: actions possible without specific human instruction

questions.text: Does the system exhibit post-deployment adaptiveness, continuous learning, or other behaviour change during use?
Who originates explicit or implicit objectives, and can the system form sub-objectives or set objectives for other systems?

data_elements.name: Autonomy level
data_elements.description: Documented degree to which the system can learn or act without human involvement after delegation.

data_elements.name: Post-deployment adaptiveness
data_elements.description: Whether the system may evolve its model or behaviour after initial development or placement.

data_elements.name: Learning mode
data_elements.description: Whether the system is trained once, periodically, or continually, including continuous learning in operation.

data_elements.name: Objective types
data_elements.description: Explicit human-defined objectives, objectives implicit in rules or policies, objectives implicit in training data, or objectives not fully known in advance.

artifacts.name: Operating envelope statement
artifacts.description: Statement of delegated autonomy, adaptiveness, learning mode and objective sources.
artifacts.identity_strategy: authoritative master-system identifier plus envelope revision

layers.name: Identity, version and intended purpose
layers.description: Stable identifiers, version lineage, intended purpose, foreseeable misuse and the geographic or market locus of operation.

findings.name: System identity and version
findings.description: The system is identified by the provider name and a system identifier and version that reflects relation to previous versions. High-risk systems in Annex III are also registered in the EU database. A date is not an identifier.

questions.text: What is the authoritative master-system identifier, and which global IRI or Dimension UUID is used if the master identifier is absent?
Under whose name or trademark is the system placed on the market or put into service, and how does that party relate to any third-party developer?
How does this version relate to previous versions, and which software or firmware versions are required to run it?

data_elements.name: Master system identifier
data_elements.description: Provider- or deployer-assigned identifier in the system of record, as used in technical documentation.

data_elements.name: System version
data_elements.description: Version of the AI system reflecting its relation to previous versions.

data_elements.name: EU database registration number
data_elements.description: Registration number assigned when the system is entered in the EU database for high-risk AI systems, where applicable.

data_elements.name: Governed global IRI
data_elements.description: IRI published when the Dimension exposes the system in an interoperable registry.

data_elements.name: Provider name
data_elements.description: Name, registered trade name or trade mark of the provider and an address at which they can be contacted.

artifacts.name: System identity record
artifacts.description: Canonical identity, version lineage and registration identifiers for the AI system.
artifacts.identity_strategy: authoritative master-system identifier of the AI system; EU registration number when issued

findings.name: Intended purpose, misuse and locus
findings.description: Intended purpose is the use intended by the provider, including context and conditions of use stated in instructions, promotional materials and technical documentation. Reasonably foreseeable misuse is use not in accordance with that purpose that may result from foreseeable human behaviour or interaction with other systems. Locus includes Union market, third-country output used in the Union, and publicly accessible space where relevant.

questions.text: What is the intended purpose, including the specific context and conditions of use declared by the provider?
What reasonably foreseeable misuse is documented, including misuse arising from interaction with other AI systems?
In which markets, jurisdictions, operational locations or publicly accessible spaces will the system operate or will its outputs be used?

data_elements.name: Intended purpose
data_elements.description: Use for which the AI system is intended by the provider, including context and conditions of use.

data_elements.name: Reasonably foreseeable misuse
data_elements.description: Documented uses not in accordance with intended purpose that may result from foreseeable human behaviour or system interaction.

data_elements.name: Market territories
data_elements.description: Jurisdictions where the system is placed on the market, put into service, or where outputs are used.

data_elements.name: Publicly accessible space use
data_elements.description: Whether the system is used in a publicly or privately owned physical place accessible to an undetermined number of persons.

artifacts.name: Instructions for use
artifacts.description: Provider information informing the deployer of intended purpose and proper use, including a basic description of the deployer user interface.
artifacts.identity_strategy: authoritative master-system identifier plus instructions revision

bundles.name: Classification, risk and context
bundles.description: Socio-technical profile of the system and the regulatory risk tier that gates obligations, including the GPAI-system versus GPAI-model boundary.
bundles.rationale: Benefits and risks differ by people, sector, data, model and task. Legal obligations then attach to prohibited practices, high-risk uses, transparency uses and general-purpose systems.

layers.name: Socio-technical profile
layers.description: OECD classification dimensions used to characterise a deployed AI system in context.

findings.name: OECD classification dimensions
findings.description: The OECD framework classifies AI systems along People and Planet, Economic Context, Data and Input, AI Model, and Task and Output. NIST AI RMF 1.0 reuses these socio-technical dimensions to map lifecycle risk. The profile characterises a deployment; it is not itself a legal risk class.

questions.text: Who uses the system, who is impacted, and what human-rights, wellbeing, labour or environmental effects are in scope?
In which industrial sector, business function and technical-maturity setting is the system deployed?
What tasks does the system perform, does it combine tasks into a composite or autonomous control system, and what action does it take on the environment?
Does this socio-technical profile justify treating the system as in-scope for heightened governance even if no high-risk legal class applies?

data_elements.name: Impacted stakeholders
data_elements.description: Individuals and groups who interact with or are affected by the applied AI system.

data_elements.name: Industrial sector
data_elements.description: Sector of deployment such as finance, health, public administration or agriculture.

data_elements.name: System tasks
data_elements.description: Tasks performed, such as recognition, event detection, forecasting, content generation or control.

data_elements.name: Human rights and wellbeing effects
data_elements.description: Documented potential effects on human rights, wellbeing, society and the world of work.

artifacts.name: Socio-technical classification profile
artifacts.description: Completed OECD-style profile of people, economic context, data, model and task for this deployment.
artifacts.identity_strategy: authoritative master-system identifier plus profile revision

layers.name: Regulatory risk class
layers.description: Legal screening against prohibited practices, high-risk classification, transparency obligations and the GPAI system boundary.

findings.name: Regulatory risk tier and prohibited practices
findings.description: The EU AI Act attaches duties by practice and use: prohibited practices, high-risk systems as safety components of Annex I products or Annex III uses, limited transparency duties, and a documented assessment where a provider considers an Annex III system not high-risk. NIST AI RMF does not use this tier taxonomy; it is contextual. Other jurisdictions may lack a statutory class.

questions.text: Has the system been screened against prohibited AI practices, and is any residual prohibited use blocked as an exception?
Is the system classified as high-risk under product-safety or Annex III rules, or has a documented not-high-risk assessment been registered?
answer_data: annex I or annex III basis

questions.text: Do chatbot, generative, emotion-recognition or other transparency obligations apply to this system independently of high-risk status?
When was the current risk class decided, and when must it be re-evaluated if intended purpose or capabilities change?

data_elements.name: Risk tier
data_elements.description: Operational class such as prohibited, high-risk, limited-transparency, or unregulated-under-this-instrument, plus any non-EU class.

data_elements.name: High-risk basis
data_elements.description: Annex I product-safety component, Annex III use, or documented not-high-risk assessment under the classification rules.

data_elements.name: Transparency obligation flags
data_elements.description: Whether Art. 50-style duties apply for interaction, synthetic content, emotion recognition or biometric categorisation.

data_elements.name: Classification event time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 time when the risk class was decided, distinct from when the Dimension ingested the decision.

artifacts.name: Risk classification record
artifacts.description: Documented prohibited-practice screen, high-risk determination or not-high-risk assessment, and transparency flags.
artifacts.identity_strategy: authoritative master-system identifier plus classification revision

findings.name: General-purpose AI system boundary
findings.description: A general-purpose AI system is an AI system based on a general-purpose AI model and capable of serving a variety of purposes, for direct use or for integration in other AI systems. The GPAI model itself is not this entity. Downstream providers integrate a model into their AI system.

questions.text: Is this record a general-purpose AI system, a single-purpose system, or a downstream system that integrates a GPAI model?
Which general-purpose or other models are integrated, and is integration vertical or contractual with another entity?
Is any integrated model still in research, development or prototyping before being placed on the market, and therefore outside GPAI-model placing rules?

data_elements.name: GPAI system flag
data_elements.description: Whether the AI system is based on a GPAI model and can serve a variety of purposes.

data_elements.name: Downstream provider flag
data_elements.description: Whether this system's provider integrates an AI model supplied by another entity or by itself.

data_elements.name: Integrated GPAI model references
data_elements.description: References to general-purpose or other models composed into this system.

artifacts.name: GPAI system-model boundary note
artifacts.description: Statement of system generality and linked model artifacts, without storing model internals.
artifacts.identity_strategy: authoritative master-system identifier plus boundary-note revision

bundles.name: Composition and dependencies
bundles.description: How the AI system is assembled from models, data and input requirements, runtime interfaces and third-party constituents, and how it relates to agents and other systems.
bundles.rationale: Technical documentation must describe architecture, pre-trained systems, data requirements, hardware, APIs and interaction with systems that are not part of the AI system itself.

layers.name: Constituent elements
layers.description: Models, data and input requirements, hardware, software interfaces and placement forms.

findings.name: Model and component composition
findings.description: Prior to deployment an AI system is typically built by combining one or more models developed manually or automatically. Technical documentation must describe architecture, pre-trained systems or tools from third parties, computational resources used to develop, train, test and validate, and forms of placement such as embedded software, downloads or APIs.

questions.text: Which model artifacts and other software or hardware components constitute this AI system, and which are explicitly not part of it?
How do software components build on or feed into each other, and what computational resources were used to develop, train, test and validate?
In which forms is the system placed on the market or put into service, such as embedded packages, downloads or APIs?

data_elements.name: Composed model references
data_elements.description: Identifiers of model artifacts used by the system, pointing at WM-SFT-004 records rather than storing weights.

data_elements.name: Architecture description
data_elements.description: How software components build on or feed into each other and integrate into overall processing.

data_elements.name: Placement forms
data_elements.description: Forms in which the AI system is placed on the market or put into service.

data_elements.name: Interacting systems not part of this system
data_elements.description: Hardware or software, including other AI systems, that this system interacts with but that are not part of it.

artifacts.name: Architecture and composition section
artifacts.description: Technical-documentation section describing models, components, architecture, resources and placement forms.
artifacts.identity_strategy: authoritative master-system identifier plus documentation revision

findings.name: Data, input and runtime interfaces
findings.description: System-level data requirements cover training, validation, testing and input data, including provenance, collection method and personal-data constraints. This finding records requirements and linkages, not the dataset sibling itself.

questions.text: What training, validation, testing and input data requirements apply at system level, including fitness for intended purpose?
What is the provenance and collection method of data and expert input used to build and operate the system?
answer_data: expert-input versus observed or synthetic data

questions.text: What personal-data, special-category or biometric constraints apply to system inputs, logs and outputs?

data_elements.name: Training data requirements
data_elements.description: System-level description of training datasets used, provenance, scope, main characteristics, labelling and cleaning, without storing the datasets.

data_elements.name: Input data specification
data_elements.description: Data provided to or acquired by the system on the basis of which it produces an output.

data_elements.name: Data and input provenance
data_elements.description: Whether data and input come from experts, are provided, observed, synthetic or derived, and whether collection is human, sensor or both.

data_elements.name: Personal data processing flag
data_elements.description: Whether the system processes personal data, special categories, or biometric data as defined in applicable law.

artifacts.name: Data requirements and datasheets section
artifacts.description: Technical-documentation datasheets describing training methodologies, dataset provenance and input specifications.
artifacts.identity_strategy: authoritative master-system identifier plus datasheet revision

layers.name: Value-chain relationships
layers.description: Third-party tools, supply-chain parties and optional agent surfaces attached to the system.

findings.name: Value chain, third parties and agents
findings.description: Responsibilities along the AI value chain can reallocate provider duties when a party puts a system into service under its own name, makes a substantial modification, or changes intended purpose. The system may expose agent actors, which remain sibling records.

questions.text: Which importers, distributors, authorised representatives, product manufacturers and downstream providers are in the value chain of this system?
Has any deployer or other operator become a provider by placing the system under its own name, making a substantial modification, or changing intended purpose?
Does the system expose one or more agent actors, and which sibling agent records are linked without duplicating agent semantics?

data_elements.name: Authorised representative
data_elements.description: Union-established person mandated to perform provider obligations, where required.

data_elements.name: Importer and distributor parties
data_elements.description: Union importer and any distributors making the system available on the market.

data_elements.name: Linked agent actors
data_elements.description: References to WM-AI-002 agent records exposed by this system.

data_elements.name: Third-party tools and pretrained systems
data_elements.description: Pre-trained systems or tools provided by third parties and how they were used, integrated or modified.

artifacts.name: Value-chain and dependency map
artifacts.description: Map of operators, third-party tools and linked agent records for the system.
artifacts.identity_strategy: authoritative master-system identifier plus value-chain revision

bundles.name: Roles, ownership and human oversight
bundles.description: Who is accountable for the system, who may authorise operation, and how humans oversee outputs and interventions.
bundles.rationale: The EU AI Act regulates providers, deployers and other operators; NIST describes AI actors across the lifecycle; ISO 42001 requires assigned roles for responsible use.

layers.name: Operator roles and ownership
layers.description: Provider, deployer and related operator identities, ownership and accountability.

findings.name: Provider, deployer and ownership
findings.description: A provider develops an AI system or has it developed and places it on the market or puts it into service under its own name or trademark. A deployer uses an AI system under its authority except in personal non-professional activity. The accountable deployer and owner in this Dimension may be the same party or different parties.

questions.text: Who is the provider and who is the deployer, and is personal non-professional use excluded from deployer duties?
Who owns the governed system record and is accountable for its responsible provision or use inside the adopting organisation?
What measures support AI literacy of providers, deployers and affected persons for this system?

data_elements.name: Provider party
data_elements.description: Natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body that places the system on the market or puts it into service under its name or trademark.

data_elements.name: Deployer party
data_elements.description: Party using the AI system under its authority, other than personal non-professional use.

data_elements.name: Accountable owner
data_elements.description: Party inside the adopting Dimension that owns the governed record and residual accountability.

data_elements.name: Operator role set
data_elements.description: Which of provider, product manufacturer, deployer, authorised representative, importer or distributor apply.

artifacts.name: Accountability and operator record
artifacts.description: Named provider, deployer, owner and other operators with contact identity.
artifacts.identity_strategy: authoritative master-system identifier plus operator-record revision

layers.name: Human oversight and authority
layers.description: Human oversight measures, intervention authority and interpretation of outputs.

findings.name: Human oversight design and authority
findings.description: High-risk AI systems must be designed so that natural persons can oversee them, interpret outputs and intervene. Technical documentation must assess oversight measures needed and technical measures that facilitate interpretation by deployers.

questions.text: What human oversight mode is implemented, and at which lifecycle stages can humans supervise, override or halt the system?
What technical measures enable deployers to interpret outputs and use them appropriately?
What happens if the designated human overseer is unavailable, overloaded or in disagreement with the system output?

data_elements.name: Oversight mode
data_elements.description: Documented human oversight arrangement, including whether a human is in, on, or over the loop where that terminology is used.

data_elements.name: Designated oversight persons
data_elements.description: Roles or persons authorised to interpret, override or halt system outputs.

data_elements.name: Override and halt capability
data_elements.description: Whether the system can be interrupted, overridden or safely stopped by a human.

data_elements.name: Output interpretation measures
data_elements.description: Technical measures facilitating deployer interpretation of outputs.

artifacts.name: Human oversight procedure
artifacts.description: Procedure describing oversight mode, authorised persons, interpretation aids and fallback.
artifacts.identity_strategy: authoritative master-system identifier plus procedure revision

bundles.name: Lifecycle, change and decommissioning
bundles.description: Stage of the AI system, events that move it between stages, substantial modification and continuous learning, and recall, withdrawal or retirement.
bundles.rationale: ISO/IEC 22989 describes evolution from inception to retirement, including continuous validation and re-evaluation. The EU AI Act adds placing on the market, putting into service, substantial modification, sandbox and real-world testing, recall and withdrawal.

layers.name: Lifecycle stages and change
layers.description: Current stage, timestamps, and whether change is a planned predetermined change or a substantial modification.

findings.name: Lifecycle stage and status
findings.description: ISO/IEC 22989 example stages include inception, design and development, verification and validation, deployment, operation and monitoring, continuous validation, re-evaluation and retirement. EU legal events include placing on the market, putting into service, sandbox participation and real-world testing that does not itself constitute placing on the market.

questions.text: What is the current lifecycle stage and operating status of this AI system?
When was the system placed on the market or put into service, and is it in a sandbox or real-world testing regime that is not placing on the market?
Have design, deployment or validation stages been re-entered for fixes, updates or re-evaluation, and under what process?

data_elements.name: Lifecycle stage
data_elements.description: Current stage such as inception, design and development, verification and validation, deployment, operation and monitoring, continuous validation, re-evaluation or retirement.

data_elements.name: Placing on the market time
data_elements.description: Event time of first making the system available on the relevant market, with offset, distinct from ingestion time.

data_elements.name: Putting into service time
data_elements.description: Event time of first supply for use to a deployer or for own use for the intended purpose.

data_elements.name: Sandbox or real-world testing flag
data_elements.description: Whether the system is under a regulatory sandbox plan or a real-world testing plan that does not constitute placing on the market.

artifacts.name: Lifecycle status record
artifacts.description: Stage, legal placement events and sandbox or real-world testing status.
artifacts.identity_strategy: authoritative master-system identifier plus lifecycle-event identifier

artifacts.name: Sandbox or real-world testing plan
artifacts.description: Sandbox plan or real-world testing plan when the system is tested under regulatory supervision.
artifacts.identity_strategy: plan identifier bound to the authoritative master-system identifier

findings.name: Substantial modification and predetermined change
findings.description: A substantial modification is a change after placing on the market or putting into service that was not foreseen in the initial conformity assessment and that affects compliance or intended purpose. Predetermined changes, including continuous learning, must be described in technical documentation with solutions that preserve compliance.

questions.text: Is a proposed or completed change a predetermined change within the assessed envelope, or a substantial modification requiring new assessment?
If the system learns in operation, what automated testing and change-control keep later versions inside certified behaviour?
When did the modification occur in the world, when was it observed, and when was conformity re-assessed?

data_elements.name: Predetermined changes
data_elements.description: Described pre-planned changes to the system and its performance, with technical solutions for continued compliance.

data_elements.name: Substantial modification flag
data_elements.description: Whether a change after placement was not foreseen in the initial assessment and affects compliance or intended purpose.

data_elements.name: Change event time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 time with seconds and offset when the change occurred, stored separately from ingestion time.

artifacts.name: Change and substantial-modification record
artifacts.description: Record of predetermined changes, substantial modifications and reassessment outcomes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: authoritative master-system identifier plus change identifier

layers.name: Recall, withdrawal and retirement
layers.description: Taking a system out of service, preventing further making available, and disposing of data and models at retirement.

findings.name: Recall, withdrawal and retirement
findings.description: Recall aims to return, take out of service or disable an AI system already made available to deployers. Withdrawal aims to prevent a system in the supply chain being made available. Retirement includes decommission, data disposal and model disposal. Documentation for high-risk systems must remain available for ten years after placement or putting into service even after retirement.

questions.text: Is the system being recalled, withdrawn, disabled, replaced or retired, and what is the trigger?
What data, model artifacts, logs and access paths are disposed of or retained at retirement?
Which post-exit duties remain, including documentation keeping, incident linkage and residual human-rights or safety monitoring?

data_elements.name: Exit mode
data_elements.description: Recall, withdrawal, disablement, replacement or retirement.

data_elements.name: Exit event time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 time when recall, withdrawal or retirement took effect, distinct from ingestion time.

data_elements.name: Documentation keep-until time
data_elements.description: Time until which technical documentation and related files remain at the disposal of competent authorities; for high-risk systems under the EU AI Act this ends 10 years after placing on the market or putting into service.

data_elements.name: Disposal actions
data_elements.description: Actions for data disposal, model disposal, decommission and discard.

artifacts.name: Recall, withdrawal or retirement record
artifacts.description: Decision, trigger, affected population, disposal actions and residual duties.
artifacts.identity_strategy: authoritative master-system identifier plus exit-event identifier

bundles.name: Assurance, transparency, access and retention
bundles.description: Risk and impact evidence, trustworthiness and performance, technical documentation and logs, access control, retention and standards alignment.
bundles.rationale: A governed AI system is operable only if risk, impact, performance, documentation, logs and access rules can be inspected and retained for the required period.

layers.name: Risk, impact and performance
layers.description: Risk management, impact assessment, and accuracy, robustness, cybersecurity and related trustworthiness characteristics.

findings.name: Risk and impact assessment
findings.description: High-risk systems require a risk-management system throughout the lifecycle. ISO/IEC 42005 guides AI system impact assessments for individuals and societies. Certain deployers of high-risk systems must perform a fundamental-rights impact assessment. Risk is the combination of probability and severity of harm.

questions.text: What reasonably foreseeable risks to health, safety, fundamental rights and discrimination are identified for the intended purpose, and how are they treated?
What AI system impact assessment or fundamental-rights impact assessment has been performed, at which lifecycle stages, and with which stakeholder input?
Which serious-incident or hazard reports name this system, without storing the incident case in this record?

data_elements.name: Identified risks
data_elements.description: Documented risks, including unintended outcomes and sources of risk to health, safety, fundamental rights and discrimination.

data_elements.name: Residual risk statement
data_elements.description: Risk remaining after treatments, against the organisation's risk tolerance.

data_elements.name: Impact assessment reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an ISO/IEC 42005-style impact assessment and, where required, an Art. 27 fundamental-rights impact assessment.

data_elements.name: Linked incident identifiers
data_elements.description: References to WM-AI-010 incident records that name this system.

artifacts.name: Risk management file
artifacts.description: Description of the risk-management system and current risk treatments for the AI system.
artifacts.identity_strategy: authoritative master-system identifier plus risk-file revision

artifacts.name: AI system impact assessment
artifacts.description: Documented assessment of impacts on individuals, groups or society, and fundamental-rights impact assessment where required.
artifacts.identity_strategy: assessment identifier bound to the authoritative master-system identifier

findings.name: Trustworthiness, performance and security
findings.description: NIST AI RMF trustworthiness characteristics include valid and reliable, safe, secure and resilient, accountable and transparent, explainable and interpretable, privacy-enhanced, and fair with harmful bias managed. High-risk systems must meet accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity requirements and declare appropriateness of performance metrics.

questions.text: Which performance metrics are used, why are they appropriate for this intended purpose, and what accuracy is expected for specific persons or groups?
What robustness, cybersecurity and resilience measures protect the system against perturbations, data poisoning, model theft or availability attacks?
How is harmful bias measured and managed for persons or groups on whom the system is intended to be used?
What verification and validation procedures, test data characteristics, test logs and signed reports demonstrate that the system meets its requirements?

data_elements.name: Performance metrics
data_elements.description: Metrics used to measure accuracy, robustness and other relevant requirements, with a statement of appropriateness.

data_elements.name: Expected accuracy
data_elements.description: Degrees of accuracy for specific persons or groups and overall expected accuracy relative to intended purpose.

data_elements.name: Cybersecurity measures
data_elements.description: Cybersecurity measures put in place for the AI system.

data_elements.name: Trustworthiness characteristic profile
data_elements.description: How the system addresses NIST-style characteristics of validity, safety, security, accountability, explainability, privacy and fairness, as alignment not claimed certification.

artifacts.name: Verification and validation reports
artifacts.description: Dated and signed test logs and reports, including tests of predetermined changes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: report identifier bound to the authoritative master-system identifier and version

layers.name: Documentation, access, retention and interoperability
layers.description: Technical documentation, logs, conformity evidence, access rules, retention and alignment to external instruments.

findings.name: Technical documentation, logs and conformity evidence
findings.description: Technical documentation for high-risk systems must exist before placing on the market or putting into service and be kept up to date. It includes general description, development process, monitoring and control information, risk-management description, lifecycle changes, applied standards, EU declaration of conformity and the post-market monitoring plan. Automatically generated logs must support record-keeping.

questions.text: Does current technical documentation contain the Annex IV elements applicable to this system, including post-market monitoring plans?
What events are automatically logged, for how long, and can logs trace operation sufficiently for post-market monitoring and oversight?
What conformity assessment procedure was applied, and where are the EU declaration of conformity, CE marking and certificates?

data_elements.name: Technical documentation revision
data_elements.description: Current revision of the technical documentation package.

data_elements.name: Log retention period
data_elements.description: Duration for which automatically generated logs are kept under the provider or deployer control.

data_elements.name: Conformity assessment procedure
data_elements.description: Internal-control or quality-management-system-plus-technical-documentation assessment, or other applicable procedure.

data_elements.name: EU declaration of conformity identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the declaration of conformity when the system is a high-risk AI system requiring one.

artifacts.name: Technical documentation
artifacts.description: Annex IV technical documentation of the AI system, kept up to date through the lifecycle.
artifacts.identity_strategy: authoritative master-system identifier plus documentation revision; content integrity hash

artifacts.name: EU declaration of conformity
artifacts.description: Declaration by which the provider states conformity with applicable high-risk requirements and other Union harmonisation legislation.
artifacts.identity_strategy: declaration identifier bound to the authoritative master-system identifier and version

artifacts.name: Post-market monitoring plan
artifacts.description: Plan for collecting and reviewing experience from use in order to identify needed corrective or preventive actions.
artifacts.identity_strategy: plan identifier bound to the authoritative master-system identifier

artifacts.name: Automatically generated logs
artifacts.description: Logs generated by the AI system to support record-keeping, oversight and post-market monitoring.
artifacts.identity_strategy: log batch or stream identifier bound to the authoritative master-system identifier and time interval

findings.name: Access, retention, deletion and interoperability
findings.description: Access to documentation and logs is restricted by default and opened to competent authorities, overseers and authorised operators. High-risk documentation is kept for ten years after placing on the market or putting into service, including bankruptcy arrangements under Member State law. External instruments are alignments; conflicts are recorded.

questions.text: Who may access technical documentation, logs, operating interfaces and impact assessments, under which scopes and with which audit trail?
How long are documentation, logs and residual operational data retained, and how are they deleted or put into escrow if the provider ceases activity?
Which external standards and legal instruments is this system aligned to, and where do those instruments conflict so that conformance is not claimed?

data_elements.name: Access policy reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the access policy governing documentation, logs and interfaces for this system.

data_elements.name: Retention periods
data_elements.description: Retention durations for technical documentation, QMS records, logs and residual data.

data_elements.name: Deletion and disposal method
data_elements.description: How residual data and access paths are deleted or disabled when retention expires or the system is retired, subject to legal holds.

data_elements.name: Alignment and conflict register
data_elements.description: List of aligned instruments and documented conflicts or non-claims of conformance.

artifacts.name: Access and retention policy binding
artifacts.description: Binding of organisational access, audit and retention rules to this AI system instance.
artifacts.identity_strategy: authoritative master-system identifier plus policy-binding revision

functions.name: Inventory and identify the AI system
functions.description: Admit a candidate as an AI system, assign or bind the master identifier and version, and record definition alignment.
preconditions: A party is prepared to place, put into service, or use the system under its authority
effects: A governed AI system record exists with an authoritative master-system identifier

functions.name: Classify context and obligations
functions.description: Complete the socio-technical profile, screen prohibited practices, assign a risk tier and GPAI-system flag, and determine applicable duties.
preconditions: System identity and intended purpose are recorded
effects: Operating permissions are gated by class; not-high-risk assessments are documented when used

functions.name: Compose the system from constituents
functions.description: Link model artifacts, data requirements, runtime interfaces, third parties and optional agent records without duplicating sibling semantics.
preconditions: Sibling model and agent identifiers resolve when cited
effects: The system record becomes an aggregate with typed edges to constituents

functions.name: Assess risk and impact
functions.description: Identify harms, treat risks, and perform or update AI system impact assessments and fundamental-rights assessments as required.
preconditions: Intended purpose and affected persons are identified
effects: Residual risk and mitigations are recorded against risk tolerance

functions.name: Authorise placing on the market or putting into service
functions.description: Confirm technical documentation, human oversight, verification and validation, and conformity evidence before first making available or first use.
preconditions: Risk class and intended purpose are current; prohibited uses are blocked
effects: Placing-on-market or putting-into-service event time is recorded; the system may be used under its envelope

functions.name: Operate with human oversight
functions.description: Run the system inside its operating envelope with designated human interpretation, override and halt paths.
preconditions: Authorised deployer and overseers are in place; access policy permits operation
effects: Outputs are produced under logged oversight; out-of-envelope use is an exception

functions.name: Monitor post-market performance
functions.description: Collect experience of use, measure drift and accuracy, and identify corrective or preventive actions, including linkage to incident reports.
preconditions: A post-market monitoring plan exists for systems that require one
effects: Performance evidence is updated; serious incidents can be referenced without absorbing the incident file

functions.name: Handle predetermined change or substantial modification
functions.description: Classify a change, keep continuous-learning systems inside their envelope, or trigger reassessment and possible reclassification.
preconditions: The system has been placed on the market or put into service, or is in operation
effects: Version lineage is updated; a substantial modification may create new provider duties or a new assessment

functions.name: Recall, withdraw or retire
functions.description: Take the system out of service or prevent further making available, dispose of residual assets, and preserve documentation for the keep-until time.
preconditions: An accountable owner or competent authority has decided an exit mode
effects: The system is no longer operable except for retained evidence access; residual duties remain

functions.name: Produce and disclose conformity evidence
functions.description: Assemble technical documentation, instructions, logs, declarations and registration data for deployers, competent authorities or the EU database.
preconditions: Identity, class and documentation revision are current
effects: An inspectable evidence package exists with integrity protection

composition.purpose: Treat the AI system as a specialised software-enabled engineered system whose distinguishing operations are inference, autonomy and possible post-deployment adaptiveness rather than duplicating generic software-system semantics.
An AI system uses one or more model artifacts as constituents; model internals remain in the model-artifact sibling.
An AI system may expose agent actors; agent identity, goals and tools remain in the agent sibling.
Incident and serious-incident reports name affected AI systems; this model stores only the linkage point.

composition.target: OECD AI system definition and classification framework
composition.purpose: Align identity and socio-technical profile to the OECD definition and the People-Planet, Economic Context, Data and Input, AI Model, and Task and Output dimensions, without claiming that alignment is legal conformance.
Align operator roles, intended purpose, risk class, technical documentation, logging, oversight, post-market monitoring, registration and retention to the AI Act where that law applies.
Align terminology and lifecycle stages to ISO/IEC 22989 while recording definitional conflicts with the OECD and EU inference-centred wording.
Align risk-management functions and trustworthiness characteristics to the voluntary NIST framework without treating it as a legal tier scheme.
Place the AI system instance under an organisational AI management system without making the AIMS itself this record.
Use AI system impact assessment guidance for individuals and societies across lifecycle stages.

composition.target: Council of Europe Framework Convention CETS 225
composition.purpose: Align lifecycle activities that may affect human rights, democracy and the rule of law, noting the national-defence exclusion.

owner_package_requirements: Designate an accountable owner and, where distinct, a provider and a deployer for every AI system record
Maintain an inventory that binds master identifier, version, intended purpose and risk class to current technical documentation
Keep model-artifact, agent-actor and incident records in their sibling models and link them with typed edges
Publish AGENTS.md so agents can locate specification, storage type, interface and processes without guessing format
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use a Dimension-owned IRI or CURIE such as vercy://dimension/{dimension-id}/ai-system/{master-system-id} rather than a storage path. Do not mint identity from dates. When an EU database number or other master-system identifier exists, bind it as the primary key and treat the Dimension UUID as a secondary key.

canonicalization_rules: Canonical identity is the authoritative master-system identifier plus version; display names and trademarks are aliases
Canonical risk class is stored as an alignment to named instruments with a conflict register, not as a single implied global enum
Composition edges to models, agents and incidents are typed references, not embedded copies
Timestamps are stored in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z
patch_rules: Patches that change intended purpose, risk class, autonomy, adaptiveness or human-oversight mode require a new version and a decision record
Predetermined changes inside the assessed envelope may patch performance parameters without a new legal placement event if documented
Substantial modifications are not silent patches; they trigger reassessment functions
Patches must record event time and ingestion time separately when they differ
compatibility_rules: A reader of an older version must still resolve provider, intended purpose and risk class
Down-revving risk class requires the not-high-risk or equivalent documented assessment, not a silent field edit
Sibling model or agent identifier changes must not break typed edges; use explicit relink patches

identity_priority: authoritative master-system identifier assigned by the provider or deployer system of record and recorded in technical documentation, including system identifier plus version and, where registered, the EU high-risk AI system database number
governed global identifier or IRI when the Dimension publishes the system in an interoperable registry
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension only when no master-system identifier or governed global identifier exists
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values SHALL be RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and an explicit offset or Z. Record event time (when the lifecycle, operational, classification or decision event occurred) separately from observation or ingestion time (when the Dimension recorded the fact) whenever those differ. A calendar date is not an identifier.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts are named {master-system-id}-{artifact-kind}-{revision-or-interval} with no embedded date-as-identity; versions increment on content change and the revision is bound to the system version they describe.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Each serial artifact SHALL carry a content integrity hash and, where a declaration, certificate or signed test report is issued, a signature or equivalent authenticity proof; replacements are new serials, not silent overwrites.

policies: External standards and laws are alignments; do not claim conformance without stored evidence.
Separate the AI system record from model artifacts, agent actors and incident files.
Default-deny access to technical documentation, logs and impact assessments except for accountable operators, designated overseers and competent authorities.
Do not operate outside the current intended-purpose and risk-class envelope; out-of-envelope use is an exception requiring a decision record.
Preserve documentation and logs for the applicable keep-until time, including the ten-year high-risk documentation duty where Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 applies.

read: Any agent holding a matching access scope may read identity, class, status and non-restricted composition
Technical documentation, logs, impact assessments and declarations require artifact-scope authorisation or competent-authority exception
Reads of restricted artifacts are audited
create: Create requires an accountable owner, a master-system identifier strategy, adopted definition alignment and an intended-purpose draft
Creation does not by itself constitute placing on the market or putting into service
update: Updates to purpose, class, autonomy, adaptiveness, oversight, composition or placement status require the handle-modification or classify-obligations function
Version lineage must be preserved; identifiers are not rewritten to dates
delete: Physical delete is forbidden while a retention hold or keep-until time is active
Logical retirement uses the recall-or-retire function; evidence remains readable to authorised roles until retention expires

roles.name: AI system owner and accountable deployer
responsibilities: Authorise intended purpose and use under organisational authority

roles.name: Provider
responsibilities: Place on the market or put into service under own name or trademark
Maintain technical documentation, logs and conformity evidence
Execute post-market monitoring and corrective actions

roles.name: Human oversight operator
responsibilities: Override or halt within the procedure

roles.name: Conformity and documentation steward
responsibilities: Keep technical documentation, V&V reports and declarations current
Bind serial artifacts to the master identifier

roles.name: Dimension registrar
responsibilities: Assign Dimension UUID or IRI only when no master identifier exists
Enforce AGENTS.md bootstrap and typed edges to sibling models

roles.name: Competent authority reader
responsibilities: Inspect documentation and logs under legal powers
Receive serious-incident linkages without becoming record owner

access.default_rule: Deny access to findings and artifacts except to the accountable owner, provider, designated overseers and Dimension registrar for identity fields; grant further access by explicit scope and risk class.
exceptions: Market surveillance and other competent authorities may access technical documentation, logs and declarations for the keep-until period
Serious-incident investigation may open otherwise restricted artifacts through the WM-AI-010 linkage
Regulatory sandbox or real-world-testing supervisors may access plans and monitoring data under the agreed plan
Whistleblowing and fundamental-rights authorities may access impact assessments as provided by applicable law
audit_requirements: Record actor, scope, artifact identifier, event time and ingestion time for every read or write of restricted artifacts
Audit changes to identity, intended purpose, risk class, oversight mode and exit mode
Retain access audit logs at least as long as the documentation they protect

read_order: current system identity and risk-class records

coverage.claim: This model covers the governed AI-enabled system as a socio-technical aggregate distinct from model artifacts, agent actors and incident files, grounded in OECD, EU, ISO/IEC, NIST and Council of Europe instruments. It is falsifiable against those texts and does not claim universal or metaphysical completeness.

checklist.notes: Master-system identifier, version, provider name, optional EU registration number, IRI and Dimension UUID/ULID, with dates excluded as identifiers.
ISO/IEC 22989 stages plus EU placing on the market, putting into service, sandbox and real-world testing, substantial modification, recall, withdrawal and retirement.
Typed composition to models and agents, value-chain operators, interacting systems not part of this system, and incident references.
RFC 3339 event versus ingestion times for classification, placement, modification and exit; keep-until time for documentation.
Version lineage, third-party pretrained systems, and data and input provenance at system level.
Provider, deployer, accountable owner and authorised representative.
Verification and validation reports, conformity assessment, declaration of conformity and performance metrics.
Default-deny scopes at bundle, layer, finding and artifact, with competent-authority and incident exceptions and audit.
Ten-year high-risk documentation keeping where the AI Act applies, log retention, retirement disposal and legal holds.
Alignments to OECD, EU AI Act, ISO/IEC 22989/42001/42005, NIST AI RMF and CETS 225 with an explicit conflict register.
OECD socio-technical profile, EU risk tiers, prohibited-practice screen, GPAI system flag and transparency duties.
Oversight mode, designated persons, interpretation measures, override and halt, and fallback exceptions.
ISO/IEC 42005 impact assessment and EU fundamental-rights impact assessment linkage.
Autonomy level, post-deployment adaptiveness, learning mode and objective origin.

known_omissions: Full ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A control catalogue and exact control numbering are not reproduced because the paid standard text was not used as a primary extract; secondary numbering of Annex A domains conflicts and is treated as a gap.
ISO/IEC 22989 full clause text for AI system 3.1.4 and human-in/on/over-the-loop definitions remains paywalled; the model uses official scope, preview terms and EU Art. 14 documentation requirements.
Sector overlays such as medical-device AI, aviation, automotive UNECE WP.29 and financial-services model risk are not expanded.
People's Republic of China generative-AI and algorithm-filing rules, Canada's AIDA, and other non-EU national bills are not modelled as classes.
AI software bill of materials formats (SPDX, CycloneDX) and the draft ISO/IEC 24970 logging standard are emerging and not treated as canonical.
Compute, energy and environmental footprint are only a People-and-Planet hint, not a measurement model.
Military and national-defence systems are excluded by CETS 225 and are not given a specialised profile.
Open-source GPAI exemptions, multi-agent systems of systems, and shadow-AI discovery methods are noted as operating risks rather than fully specified findings.
conflicts: ISO/IEC 22989:2022 defines an engineered system generating outputs for human-defined objectives, without the OECD/EU/CoE verb infers and without stressing post-deployment adaptiveness in the definition sentence.
NIST AI RMF 1.0 still uses an older OECD-like definition that omits content as an output type and the infers wording of the 2023 OECD revision.

Secondary summaries of ISO/IEC 22989 sometimes list seven lifecycle stages and omit continuous validation; the ANSI preview table of contents lists eight stages including continuous validation and re-evaluation.
The EU AI Act uses a product-safety risk-tier scheme; NIST AI RMF uses contextual, non-tiered risk and must not be treated as equivalent classification.
A general-purpose AI model is not an AI system; collapsing the two would break Chapter V versus Chapter III duties.
An ISO/IEC 42001 AIMS is an organisational management system, not the AI system instance it governs.

Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) amended some application dates and literacy wording; it did not rewrite the AI system definition used here, but date-sensitive operating calendars must be checked against the consolidated act.
regional_assumptions: The EU AI Act is treated as the most operational legally binding product-safety-style regime for system duties, not as a global law.
The OECD definition is treated as the intergovernmental alignment hub used by the EU and the Council of Europe.
NIST AI RMF 1.0 is treated as a voluntary United States-origin framework usable by any organisation, not as a statutory class.
Council of Europe CETS 225 is treated as a human-rights, democracy and rule-of-law overlay on lifecycle activities, with national defence out of scope.
ISO/IEC 22989, 42001 and 42005 are treated as international terminology, management-system and impact-assessment alignments that organisations may adopt regardless of jurisdiction.
adversarial_checks: Would a rules-only calculator or OCR pipeline be wrongly admitted as an AI system, or a genuinely inferential system excluded because it is simple?
Would a GPAI model record be stored here instead of as WM-SFT-004, hiding Chapter V duties?
Would an agent persona be stored here instead of as WM-AI-002, hiding actor-level controls?
Would fine-tuning, prompt-level productisation, or putting a third-party system under a new trademark silently fail to trigger provider duties or substantial-modification assessment?
Would continuous learning after deployment invalidate placement-time assurances without a predetermined-change envelope?
Would a third-country system whose outputs are used in the Union escape inventory because the provider is not established in the Union?
Would shadow or unsanctioned deployments exist outside this inventory while still affecting persons?
Would research, sandbox or personal non-professional use be over- or under-classified as placing on the market or as deployer use?
